target_questions.question: Does a reflected shock selectively suppress radial spray growth and mixing without materially changing tip penetration?
target_questions.target_basis: Tier 2 D005 links shock-wave generation to spray structure; this paper isolates reflected-wave influence.

evidence_candidates.claim_text: Schlieren experiments show that reflected shocks suppress radial spray growth, cone angle, volume, and air entrainment while having little effect on spray-tip penetration.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: N2 and SF6 atmospheres and injection-angle comparisons separate radial-interface deformation from axial penetration.

core_links.shared_parameter_or_mechanism: shock-wave effects on diesel-spray penetration and angle

limitations: Engine-inspired chamber and reflected-wave configuration; the result is not equivalent to isolated-droplet planar-shock loading.
visual_verification: Targeted visual verification performed where numeric/glyph-dependent abstract claims required it; no figure digitization.
